title: The Jew Among Thorns

full_text:
An honest servant worked faithfully for three years for a skinflint master, who at the end of the term handed him a meager pittance of three copper farthings. The cheerful lad took the small coins without anger, praising the master and heading singing down the highway.

In the forest, he met an elderly wanderer who begged for alms. The generous youth gave away all three copper coins without hesitation. In gratitude, the wanderer granted him three wishes: a magical crossbow that never missed its mark, a fiddle that forced anyone hearing it to dance, and the power that no one could refuse his first request.

Further along the path, he met an avaricious, dishonest merchant who stood gazing covetously at a singing thrush perched high in a thick briar bush. The youth shot the bird with his bow, and it fell into the center of the dense thorn hedge. When the greedy merchant scrambled in to grab it, the youth began playing his magic fiddle.

Instantly, the merchant was compelled to dance wildly, leaping and hopping among the sharp thorns, tearing his coat and crying for mercy. He begged the youth to stop, tossing him a bag of gold coins before being released.

Furious at his humiliation, the merchant ran to the judge, falsely accusing the boy of being a violent highway robber who had beaten him and stolen his gold. The youth was dragged to the gallows. Before the rope was tightened, the boy made his final request: to play one last tune upon his violin.

As the first lively notes rang out, the judge, the executioner, the bailiffs, the horses, and the deceitful merchant all burst into an uncontrollable, frantic jig, dancing in circles until they were completely exhausted. The judge begged him to cease, promising him total pardon. The terrified merchant confessed his slanderous lies, and the merry lad walked free with honor and joy.
moral: Generosity and cheerfulness gain magical aid, while greed and false accusations fall into their own traps.

quiz.question: What is the central moral lesson taught in "The Jew Among Thorns"?
options: Presence of mind and quiet wisdom triumph over brute strength.
Acting in haste and anger without thinking
Believing rumors and flattery without proof
quiz.hint: Remember the moral lesson of this traditional story.

quiz.question: How do the characters overcome their challenge?
options: Through patience, calm reflection, and wisdom
By shouting loudly and blaming others
By running away from every problem
quiz.hint: Consider the virtues praised in world folklore.

quiz.question: What memorable conclusion does this story teach young readers?
options: Honesty, kindness, and clear thinking lead to peace
quiz.hint: Reflect upon the resolution of the story.
